derivation.two_body_potential: V_pi(q) = -(f/m_pi)^2 tau1.tau2 [gamma5 gamma^i]_1 [gamma5 gamma^j]_2 ( q^i q^j D(q) - g' delta^ij ), D = 1/(q_vec^2 + m_pi^2), static (q0 = 0 in vertex and propagator); nonrelativistic limit -(f/m_pi)^2 tau1.tau2 (sigma1.q)(sigma2.q)/(q^2+m_pi^2) + g' (f/m_pi)^2 sigma1.sigma2 tau1.tau2 (OPEP + Landau-Migdal contact)
derivation.spin_traces: T_pi(k,k') = sum_{ss'} [ubar_k gamma5 qslash u_k'][ubar_k' gamma5 qslash u_k] = [ (k^2+k'^2)(EE'+M*^2) - 2 k^2 k'^2 + (k.k') (k^2+k'^2 - 2(EE'+M*^2)) ]/(EE') (u^dagger u = 1, q = k - k'); T_ii = sum_i sum_{ss'} [ubar gamma5 gamma^i u'][ubar' gamma5 gamma^i u] = 3 + (3 M*^2 - k.k')/(EE'); NR limits 2 q^2 and 6
derivation.isospin: Fock weights c_nn = c_pp = 1, c_np = c_pn = 2 (tau1.tau2 = 2 P_tau - 1); symmetric matter total 6 = 3 x isoscalar
derivation.energy_density: eps_pi = f^2/(8 pi^4 m_pi^2) sum_{ij} c_ij int_0^{k_i} dk int_0^{k_j} dk' k^2 k'^2 { [C0 Theta + C1 k k' Phi]/(EE') - g' (3 + 3 M*^2/(EE')) }, C0 = (k^2+k'^2)(EE'+M*^2) - 2k^2k'^2, C1 = k^2+k'^2 - 2(EE'+M*^2), Theta = <1/(A-Bx)>, Phi = <x/(A-Bx)>, A = k^2+k'^2+m_pi^2, B = 2kk' (session kernels fock_exchange.theta_phi)
derivation.contact_part_closed_form: eps_contact = -(3 g' f^2/(8 m_pi^2)) sum_ij c_ij (n_i n_j + rho_s,i rho_s,j)
derivation.functional: eps(n, delta, y) = chain functional [+ sigma/omega Fock of missing/fock] + eps_pi ; y re-stationarised (d eps/dy = 0); mu_i = d eps/dn_i ; P = sum n_i mu_i - eps ; S = (1/2n) d^2 eps/d delta^2 ; L = 3 n dS/dn ; K = 9 dP/dn

rmf_control.literature_comparison: RHF literature (from memory, not verifiable offline): the kernels used here coincide with the standard RHF pseudovector-pion functions A_pi = B_pi = -f_pi^2 Theta_pi, C_pi = 2 (f_pi/m_pi)^2 [(p^2+p'^2) Phi_pi - p p' Theta_pi] (Bouyssy, Mathiot, Van Giai, Marcos, PRC 36, 380 (1987)), i.e. the zero-range term removed. PKO1 (Long, Van Giai, Meng, PLB 640, 150 (2006)) uses f_pi(0) = 1.0 (f^2/4pi = 0.0796) with a fitted quenching exp(-a_pi rho/rho0), a_pi = 1.232, so that at saturation the pion strength is 8.5 percent of the free one and its Fock energy is below 1 MeV per nucleon; scaling the present free-coupling result by that factor gives E_pi/A = -0.57 MeV and S_pi = +0.29 MeV at the DD-ME2 saturation point, the size RHF papers describe (small pion contribution to bulk matter, large sigma/omega Fock contributions to the symmetry energy). With the free coupling 0.075 the pion Fock term is -6.3 MeV (zero-range removed) or +14.1 MeV (kept) per nucleon at M*/M = 0.57.

caveats: First order in the exchange with Hartree spinors and a re-stationarised scalar field; the momentum dependence of full RHF enters only through first-order self-energies in the spin-orbit test.

Only the Fock term was computed. Second-order pion exchange (iterated one-pion exchange, tensor correlations, two-pion exchange with Delta) is the main pion contribution to binding and to the symmetry energy in ab-initio and chiral calculations; it needs at least one regulator and is outside a zero-parameter mean-field-plus-Fock test. The verdict covers the Fock level only.
Static propagator and vertex, point vertices (no form factor), free pion mass at all densities.

The zero-range treatment is a discrete choice with opposite signs of the result: -6.2 MeV per nucleon and +3.3 MeV in S for g' = 1/3, +15.9 MeV and -4.3 MeV for g' = 0. The primary choice was declared before computing.
Bookkeeping R keeps the empirical J and L by re-deriving the rho contact; it is not a zero-parameter isovector sector. The zero-parameter version (Z) fails both anchors.

The a5_min members sit on the stability edge (q_min = 0 to rounding), like the original island member. The shifted island member (y* = 0.8507) is a new member, compared with a no-pion control at the same y*.

Literature magnitudes (Bouyssy et al. 1987 kernels, PKO1 coupling and quenching, Nijmegen f^2, the closed form of the one-pion-exchange Fock energy) are quoted from memory; no internet. The numerical checks do not depend on them.
Full-RHF 'medium'-mass variant: the forward check fails for the quintic members (K 262.8 instead of 260 for the corner, Q0 mismatch), so it is reported in pion_jet.json but not used.
Spin-orbit numbers come from the validated LDA procedure (first-order splitting with Woods-Saxon-fitted wave functions); the pion tensor term was not computed for 208Pb.
R3 (surface) and R4 (crust) were not computed with the pion.
verdict_text: With its measured coupling and zero unknown parameters, the pion Fock term is not the missing element for R1 or for R2. R1: with the zero-range term removed it adds +3.3 MeV to S(n0) (13.4-14.6 -> 16.7-18.0 MeV; L = 36.5-42.7 MeV), 18 percent of the +18 MeV needed; with the zero-range term kept it subtracts 4.3 MeV. At the full RHF level of the action (its own scalar and vector Fock terms plus the pion) S(n0) = 12.6-13.3 MeV, below the Hartree value. Without the empirical contact neutron matter is bound at 0.10 fm^-3. R2: the pion self-energies give Sigma_0 - Sigma_S = -0.15 MeV where +400 to +480 MeV is needed; the 16O 1p splitting goes from 1.04-1.48 to 0.95-1.38 MeV. The stability bound moves the wrong way (m*/M >= 0.8358 becomes >= 0.8465), and the declared island member at y* = 0.84 and the quartic at 0.87 lose global stability. R5 and the joint likelihood do not improve (chi2 13.88 -> 14.73 for the island-type member; J0614 radius z +2.4, J0740 mass z -1.2). The sub-saturation anchors survive only if the empirical isovector contact is re-fitted around the pion. The declared alternative (zero-range term kept) closes the forbidden effective-mass band and reaches 16O 1p = 4.4 MeV at m*/M = 0.65, still below the window, while making R1 worse; that choice is disfavoured by Gamow-Teller systematics (g' about 0.6).
